## Claims
- [source-backed] The lower-adjoined family generates \(J_v\), and the 2024 theorem proves its minimality over \(\mathbb Z\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- [source-backed] The claimed no-syzygy theorem is deduced from Theorem 4.4; it is the essential input used to upgrade minimal generation to integral independence. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 790-831]
- [proved] Assuming that no-syzygy theorem, the lower-adjoined residues are an integral homogeneous basis of \(J_v/A_+J_v\): a homogeneous kernel relation is exactly a prohibited syzygy; hence no torsion remains. The grading is Schur degree (ordinary cohomological degrees are twice these).
- [proved] The first missing certificate is the large-\(N\) descent in Theorem 4.4: one needs
  \[
  P\bigl(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau)\bigr)\in
  \operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu):
  \nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\varphi}\text{ wide}\}
  \]
  for every wide \(\tau\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\widehat\varphi}\), where \(P\) kills the enlarged variables. This is not supplied.
- [proved] Lemma 4.3 verifies only
  \(P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\widehat\nu))
   =\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu)\)
  for originally indexed \(\nu\); it does not control the additional wide enlarged equations. Therefore inconsistency of the enlarged system does not, by itself, imply inconsistency of the original subsystem. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 777-818]
- [proved] Conditional on the lower integral-basis result, conjugation is otherwise sound: \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) sends \(I_{r,q}\) to \(I_{q,r}\), preserves Schur degree and \(A_+\), and sends the interval above \(i^j\) to that above \(j^i\). The parameter translation
  \[
  v^\vee=v_{q,\ q+j-i,\ q-i+1,\ n},\qquad
  (i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b)
  \]
  satisfies the bigrassmannian inequalities.
- [proved] Under that conditional quotient isomorphism, conjugating
  \((j^i,\rho)\), \(\rho\subseteq b^a\), gives
  \[
  (j^i,\rho)'=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b}),
  \]
  exactly the right-adjoined family. Its generation follows from graded Nakayama since \(A_+\) is nilpotent in \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\).

## Strategy
The audit passes the parameter translation, conjugation map, grading, and the conditional Nakayama/torsion arguments. It fails first at the cited proof’s enlargement-and-restriction step: the required projected-wide-row certificate is absent. No repair can be derived from the supplied excerpt because the needed control of all additional \(\widehat\varphi\)-wide rows is neither stated nor proved.

## Gaps
The requested target is **not established** by this audit. The lower integral-basis theorem remains unsupported until the projected-wide-row certificate above is proved; consequently the quotient-conjugation and right-adjoined theorems remain conditional. No counterexample to the theorems themselves is exhibited.

## Next
Prove the displayed projected-wide-row certificate, including an explicit classification of every enlarged wide row surviving \(P\).
